page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). It also features 550 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Graphical processing units are not present on this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show top-quartile parallel processing capability. The system achieves strong scores in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (86,554.16), Geekbench multi-core execution (17,481.0), and PassMark CPU evaluations (52,836.15). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 305.06 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Hardware cryptography is reinforced by dedicated instruction support including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, reflected in a high PassMark encryption rating of 63,191.42. Compute-heavy operations such as Clang compilation (38,793.0) and ray tracing (62,663.0) similarly fall within top performance percentiles. Cached memory reads register at 4,138.02 GB/sec, although large-block uncached memory throughput operates in the middle 50% tier with 98.35 GB/sec for reads and 49.74 GB/sec for writes.

Single-thread metrics maintain solid mid-tier performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,608.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 25.85 GB/sec. Instruction support encompasses standard AVX, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but lacks modern AVX-512 extensions and AMX units. CPU-based inference reflects these trade-offs: small model handling (135M parameters) executes in the top 25% at 2,387.88 prompt tokens per second, but larger language models (7B and 70B) shift toward average throughput due to the absence of specialized tensor or vector extensions.

Balancing 64 dedicated compute threads with 256 GB of memory and local solid-state storage provides significant density and compute capacity without the premium associated with specialized accelerator hardware. Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 fits multi-threaded enterprise workloads, including large-scale software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, relational databases, static web clusters, and multi-user application servers.
description: Microsoft Azure D64as_v4 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 256.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 550 GB of local SSD storage, without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core computational performance, posting 17,481.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 52,836.15 in PassMark CPU, and 86,554.16 in stress-ng multi-core workloads. Dedicated hardware cryptographic acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI) yields high cryptographic throughput, complemented by strong software compilation and ray-tracing metrics. Single-thread processing and large uncached memory transfers rank within the middle tier. The instance provides a dense, cost-efficient allocation of general-purpose compute and memory capacity for enterprise application hosting, batch ETL jobs, software build clusters, and databases.
